title: At the window (Confessions 9.10)
hook: Augustine and Monica, rising in thought beyond all things
carry: we touched it for a moment
tomorrow: where do you keep the smell of lilies in a dark room?

segments.voice: A child's chant, a few lines of Romans, and the long wavering ended. Your line: take up and read. Today the story slows down, at a window.

Some of the best talks happen side by side: in a car at night, on a porch, at the kitchen sink, nobody looking at anybody. Ostia, on the Tiber. Augustine and his mother, Monica, are resting from a long journey before a sea voyage. One day the two of them are leaning at a window over the garden of the house where they're staying. No crowd, no noise. A mother and her son, talking quietly. And the talk keeps climbing.
screen: `SIDE BY SIDE.` → `OSTIA, ON THE TIBER.` → `THE TALK KEEPS CLIMBING.`

segments.voice: They're talking about the life of the saints to come, the life Paul describes this way: "Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard." Step by step their thoughts rise, past everything bodily, past the earth, the sun, the moon and the stars, to their own minds, and beyond those too, toward the wisdom by which everything was made. And there, Augustine says, while they spoke of it and longed for it, they touched it, a little, with one whole beat of the heart. That's the answer to yesterday's question. Then they sighed, and came back down to the sound of their own voices, where every word has a beginning and an end. Then Monica speaks. Son, she says, for my part nothing in this life delights me anymore. There was one thing I wanted to stay for: to see you a Catholic Christian before I died. God has given me that, and more. What am I doing here still? Not long after, Augustine tells us, she fell ill. Here's the detail to keep: this talk doesn't happen in a church. It happens at a window, between two people, and neither of them has all the words.
screen: `EYE HATH NOT SEEN.` · `PAST THE SUN, MOON AND STARS.` · `ONE WHOLE BEAT OF THE HEART.` · `WHAT AM I DOING HERE STILL?` · then, large: `WE TOUCHED IT FOR A MOMENT.`

segments.voice: Pick up your phone and send one person a real question, not small talk: what do you hope heaven is like, or what's the most beautiful thing you've ever seen? Then set the phone face down and sit, whether or not they've answered.
At the window. Augustine and Monica at Ostia, talking about the life to come until they touched it, for one heartbeat.
Keep this close: we touched it for a moment, and then came back down to words. Rest easy.

chat.meaning: Augustine and Monica didn't need every answer. They talked and longed together at a window, and touched it for a moment.

Ostia.meaning: a port town near Rome, at the mouth of the Tiber

Tiber.meaning: the river that runs through Rome

Catholic Christian.meaning: here, a member of the worldwide church of that time

Beats from 9.10: at Ostia on the Tiber, resting from a long journey before the voyage; leaning at a window over the garden; talk of the eternal life of the saints, which 'eye hath not seen' (1 Cor 2:9, quoted by Augustine); rising beyond bodily things, heaven, sun, moon and stars, to their own minds and beyond; touching wisdom 'with one whole beat of the heart'; returning to speech that begins and ends; the 'if all were silent' passage (now in the trapdoor only); Monica's words about seeing him a Catholic Christian. Confirm each.
9.11 says she fell ill 'scarce five days after, or not much more'; the script says only 'not long after' to avoid an unchecked count.

The Monica speech is a close paraphrase; confirm it is faithful. 'Catholic Christian' follows the text; the gloss explains it as the worldwide church of the time. A Keeper on this broad path may want to check that framing.
